title: Kohli Tore His Hamstring in the IPL Final. He Played Through It. Now He Will Miss All Three Afghanistan ODIs.
excerpt: Yashasvi Jaiswal replaces India's ODI linchpin after the RCB star battled through a hamstring tear to win the title. The England tour is in doubt too.
body:
Virat Kohli will not play a single minute of India's first-ever bilateral ODI series against Afghanistan. The BCCI confirmed on Saturday that the 37-year-old has been ruled out of all three matches -- in Dharamshala, Lucknow, and Chennai -- after sustaining a hamstring injury during the IPL 2026 final on May 31.

Kohli battled through the pain that evening in Ahmedabad, producing a match-winning 75 not out off 42 deliveries as Royal Challengers Bengaluru clinched their second consecutive title against Gujarat Titans. The innings sealed the Player of the Match award, but it also sealed his absence from India's next assignment.

## The Replacement

Chief selector Ajit Agarkar named Yashasvi Jaiswal as Kohli's replacement. The 24-year-old left-hander has played only four ODIs so far but carries serious credentials: a maiden century against South Africa last December, and an average of 57 in the format.

"Yashasvi Jaiswal will replace Virat Kohli for the three ODIs against Afghanistan," Agarkar said during the squad announcement in Mumbai.

Jaiswal is currently with the Test squad in Mullanpur, where he opened alongside KL Rahul against Afghanistan. He scored 24 before being caught behind off Mohammad Saleem in the first session on Day 1. With the Test wrapping up on Day 3, he will have time to switch gears before the first ODI on June 13.

## Recovery Timeline

Reports suggest Kohli's hamstring tear could take up to six weeks to heal fully. That timeline puts his availability for the England ODI series -- beginning July 14 in Birmingham -- in doubt.

Agarkar was cautiously optimistic. "Less than a week since he injured himself in the final," he said. "He's been assessed, but it looks like he'll be fit for the England series. I don't have a definitive answer yet."

## What It Means for the NRI Calendar

For diaspora fans who had circled the Afghanistan ODIs as their chance to watch Kohli in action before the England tour, the news is a blow. The three matches were meant to be Kohli's return to international cricket after a six-month gap since the New Zealand ODIs in January, where he scored 240 runs at a strike rate of 105.

Former India cricketer Atul Wassan offered a contrarian view. "I'm actually happy with this news," he told ANI. "It would have been overkill if Virat played every single series going forward to the next World Cup. Looking at the intensity on his body during the IPL and him playing in this heat at his age, I think it would have been pragmatic for him to take a backseat anyway."

## What Comes Next

India's ODI squad for the Afghanistan series now reads: Rohit Sharma (captain), Shubman Gill, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul, Hardik Pandya, Ishan Kishan, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Prasidh Krishna, and others. The first ODI is on June 13 in Dharamshala, followed by Lucknow on June 17 and Chennai on June 20. Rohit and Hardik's participation still depends on fitness clearances from the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.

For NRI fans in the US and UK tracking India's ODI World Cup 2027 preparations, Jaiswal's inclusion is the real storyline. He proved in December that he belongs in the ODI setup. Three matches against Afghanistan -- on Indian soil, in Indian conditions, with a spot in the England touring party at stake -- could cement him as Kohli's long-term understudy in the format. At 24, he has time. At 37, Kohli does not play every series anymore. The transition, whenever it arrives, has a face.

The Afghanistan ODI series will be broadcast on Star Sports in India and streamed on JioHotstar. NRI viewers in North America can catch all three matches on Willow TV.
